name: blocks-editor
title: Block programming
tagline: Block programs that really run, Scratch-grade: sprites, events, loops, clones, sound, lists and custom blocks; task-sized toolbox, Parsons tray, run-marked answers.
description: A block programming environment in the register KS2/3 computing actually teaches, with the whole Scratch 3 core palette and Pen underneath. A project is a stage and one or more sprites, each with scripts headed by hats (when ▶ clicked, when a key is pressed, when clicked, when I receive, when the timer passes, when I start as a clone, custom-block definitions). Run executes them for real with a frame scheduler that behaves like the real thing — 30 frames a second, loops that yield each pass, parallel scripts taking turns, waits and glides on the clock — and draws everything from the run: movement, pen ink and stamps, say and think bubbles, costume changes, graphic effects, clones, backdrops, sounds, variable and list watchers. Step walks one block at a time; the speed dial runs from "watch" (a block every 0.7 s, each one acted out) to turbo; Stop is the stop sign. Nothing on the stage is authored: a figure OPENS UNRUN — sprites at their starting poses — on screen and on paper, so nothing is answered before a pupil presses anything. Every white slot, dropdown and colour is editable in place on the data dial; editable: true adds a Build tab whose palette is TASK-SIZED — derived from the marking key on a marked figure (the categories, the block types, or a Parsons tray of the answer's own pieces) — with drag-and-drop across scripts, make-a-variable / list / block, adding sprites, and a full-screen builder for open-ended projects. An optional panel (show.text) prints the same program as AQA pseudo-code when it has an AQA reading. Marked answers: run-figure (the drawing must make a shape) and run-program (the program must behave like a reference over tests). Original sprites, costumes, backdrops and sounds; collisions are shape-based.
whenToUse: Reach for this whenever a lesson wants pupils to READ, RUN, EDIT or BUILD a block program rather than look at a screenshot of one: KS2/KS3 sequence, selection and iteration in the block-code register, events and broadcasts, animation with costumes, games (forever loops, key presses, touching, score variables, clones), lists, custom blocks, predict-the-output, fix-the-bug, pen drawing, and the blocks-to-text transition. TWO SHAPES: `script` (+ `sprite`, `start`) for ONE sprite with ONE green-flag script — most figures; `sprites` (+ `stage`) for anything more — several sprites, other hats, custom blocks, backdrops. Conventions: direction 90 = right; the pen starts UP (put pen down first) and 3 wide; variables start at 0 and lists empty, for all sprites, and get watchers (show.variables / show.lists); an ask STOPS its script until the pupil types — it cannot be pre-answered on the figure (to fix a value, set a variable instead); pick random is seeded by `seed`; Run always restarts from the authored start, so a run is reproducible. Name other sprites exactly as their `name` (default the capitalised character). Common configurations: worked example — a short program on the "data" dial (the default), pupils press Run and retune values; predict-the-output — editable: false with show.controls: false, the same program WITH controls in the explanation; build-it — editable: true, marked with run-figure (markFigure: a shape) or run-program (markProgram: a reference + tests), toolbox left to derive from the key; Parsons — toolbox "pieces" (the answer's own blocks, each used once; add `distractors` to taunt); a fix-it task — the buggy program on editable: true with a key, so the palette offers what the fix needs; open-ended projects — editable: true with toolbox "all" (the default when unmarked) and the full-screen builder. A figure is a stage, not an IDE: a dozen blocks per script reads well on a slide; the scripts column shows ONE sprite at a time (a strip under the stage switches). This model owns its run state: no staged `steps`, no draggable params — sequence blocks for predict → run → discuss. Synonyms: blocks, block code, visual programming, Scratch-style coding, sprite, stage, costume, backdrop, broadcast, forever, clone, when flag clicked, my blocks, custom block, game, animation.

expr.description: A value slot: a plain number, string or boolean, or a reporter block object that computes one. Reporters nest.

op.description: x: "x position". y: "y position". direction: "direction". size: "size". volume: "volume". answer: "answer" — the last reply typed. mouse-down: "mouse down?". mouse-x: "mouse x". mouse-y: "mouse y". timer: "timer" — seconds since Run (or since reset timer). days-since-2000: "days since 2000".

prop.description: Report the number (1-based) or the name.

what.description: "edge", "mouse-pointer", or the name of another sprite in the project (touching any of its clones counts too).

op.description: touching-color: "touching color [ ]?" — against pen ink, stamps, other sprites and the backdrop (a backdrop colour counts only where it is the top paint, so a sprite on the grass is not touching the sky behind it).
color-touching: "color [ ] is touching [ ]?" — the first colour is part of this sprite.

to.description: "mouse-pointer", or the name of another sprite in the project.

key.description: A key: "space", "up arrow", "down arrow", "left arrow", "right arrow", "any", a letter a–z or a digit 0–9.

prop.description: For a sprite: "x position", "y position", "direction", "costume #", "costume name", "size", "volume", or one of that sprite's own variables. For "Stage": "backdrop #", "backdrop name", "volume", or a variable for all sprites.

unit.description: Part of the current date and time (inside marking runs the date is fixed, so it is reproducible).

op.description: add: a + b (non-numbers count as 0). sub: a − b. mul: a × b. div: a / b (÷0 gives Infinity). mod: a mod b — floored, taking the sign of b.
random: "pick random (from) to (to)" — SEEDED by `seed`; whole-number bounds give a whole number.
gt: a > b (numbers numerically, text case-insensitively). lt: a < b. eq: a = b. join: "join (a) (b)" — both as text, stuck together.

fn.description: The maths function. Trig works in DEGREES.

name.description: The variable's name, e.g. "score". Variables need no declaring: a name used here starts at 0, for all sprites, unless declared in a sprite's `variables`.

op.description: list: A list's contents as text.

block.description: One statement block. Categories: motion, looks, sound, events, control, sensing, operators, variables, lists, my blocks, pen.

to.description: "random position", "mouse-pointer", or the name of another sprite in the project.

op.description: go-to: "go to x: ( ) y: ( )" — jump there (the pen draws the jump if down).
glide-to-target: "glide (secs) secs to (…)" — moves smoothly over that time.

to.description: "random position", "mouse-pointer", or the name of another sprite in the project.

op.description: point: "point in direction ( )" — 0 up, 90 right, 180 down, −90 left.
point-towards: "point towards (mouse-pointer / random direction / a sprite)".

towards.description: "mouse-pointer", "random direction", or the name of another sprite in the project.

op.description: change-x: "change x by ( )". change-y: "change y by ( )". change-size: "change size by ( )" (percent). change-volume: "change volume by ( )". change-pen-size: "change pen size by ( )".

op.description: set-x: "set x to ( )". set-y: "set y to ( )". set-size: "set size to ( ) %". set-volume: "set volume to ( ) %". set-pen-size: "set pen size to ( )" (the pen starts 3 wide).

bounce: "if on edge, bounce". next-costume: "next costume" — in a loop it animates (the five characters' costumes are walk frames). next-backdrop: "next backdrop". clear-effects: "clear graphic effects". show: "show". hide: "hide" — a hidden sprite still runs its scripts (and still draws with the pen). stop-sounds: "stop all sounds". clear-sound-effects: "clear sound effects". delete-clone: "delete this clone" — ends its stack; nothing happens on an original sprite. reset-timer: "reset timer". erase-all: "erase all". stamp: "stamp" — leaves a picture of the sprite on the pen layer. pen-down: "pen down" — the pen starts UP; while down, every move draws. pen-up: "pen up".
say-for: "say ( ) for ( ) seconds" — the bubble clears after that time. think-for: "think ( ) for ( ) seconds" — a thought cloud.

say: "say ( )" — the bubble stays until replaced; say "" clears it. What is said is the program's OUTPUT. A typed value shows as typed; a COMPUTED number that is not whole shows to two decimal places, as the real thing shows it (say (10 / 3) says 3.33). think: "think ( )".

op.description: call: Run a custom block this sprite DEFINES (a script with when: "define"); args fill its inputs in order.

proc.description: The custom block's name — the `proc` of this sprite's "define" script.

args.description: Values for the definition's inputs, in order.

script.description: One script: a HAT (`when`) and the blocks under it. Omit `when` for a loose stack that never runs by itself.

when.description: The hat: "flag" (when ▶ clicked — Run fires it), "key" (when [key] key pressed — needs `key`), "clicked" (when this sprite / the stage is clicked), "backdrop" (when backdrop switches to — needs `backdrop`), "timer" (when timer > `value` seconds), "receive" (when I receive — needs `message`), "clone" (when I start as a clone — sprites only), "define" (a custom block — needs `proc`; `params` and `warp` optional).

key.description: A key: "space", "up arrow", "down arrow", "left arrow", "right arrow", "any", a letter a–z or a digit 0–9.

message.description: The broadcast message name, e.g. "game over". Messages need no declaring: any name used here and in a "receive" hat is the same message.

backdrop.description: For a "backdrop" hat: the backdrop name.

value.description: For a "timer" hat: the seconds the timer must pass.

proc.description: For "define": the custom block's name, e.g. "draw square". Calls name it in `proc`.

params.description: For "define": the block's inputs, in order. Read them inside the definition with { op: "arg", name }.

warp.description: For "define": "run without screen refresh" — its loops do not wait for the screen, so the whole block runs in one frame.

blocks.description: A sequence of blocks, run top to bottom. May be empty (an empty C-mouth).

name.description: The sprite's name (default: its character, capitalised). Other blocks name it this way: touching, go to, of, create clone of. Unique; not "Stage", "edge", "mouse-pointer", "random position" or "myself".

character.description: Who it is — ORIGINAL art. Five characters (robot, penguin, frog, rocket, invader) whose costumes -a/-b/-c are walk frames, and props for games: ball (costumes ball-blue/-green/-red/-yellow/-purple), apple (apple-red/-green), star (star, star-glow), paddle, heart (heart, heart-empty), arrow, button (button, button-pressed).

costume.description: Starting costume — a costume name (e.g. "ball-red") or a 1-based number. Default the first.

draggable.description: Pupils can drag it on the stage while the program runs (default false).

variables.description: Declared variables and their starting values, e.g. { "score": 0 }. Undeclared names used by blocks start at 0 anyway.

lists.description: Declared lists and their starting items, e.g. { "fruit": ["apple", "kiwi"] }.

stage.description: The stage: its backdrops, its own scripts, and the variables and lists for all sprites.

backdrops.description: The backdrop list, in order (default ["plain"]). Original art: plain, sky, night, space, grass (ground from y −60 down), sea (water up to y 20), maze (slate walls #5c6672, a green goal patch bottom-right), desert.

backdrop.description: The starting backdrop — a name from the list or a 1-based number (default the first).

scripts.description: The stage's scripts (no motion blocks: the stage does not move).

variables.description: Declared variables and their starting values, e.g. { "score": 0 }. Undeclared names used by blocks start at 0 anyway.

lists.description: Declared lists and their starting items, e.g. { "fruit": ["apple", "kiwi"] }.

script.description: The ONE-SPRITE shape: the program as one green-flag script (drawn under a "when ▶ clicked" hat). Use with `sprite` and `start`. An empty array poses just the hat — the blank answer space for a build task (editable: true). For several sprites, other hats or custom blocks use `sprites` instead.

sprite.description: The one-sprite shape's character (default robot). See sprites[].character for the cast.

start.description: The one-sprite shape's starting pose. Default (0, 0) facing 90.

direction.description: Starting heading: 0 up, 90 right (default), 180 down, −90 left.

sprites.description: The PROJECT shape: every sprite, back to front, each with its own scripts. The first sprite's scripts show on load.

seed.description: Seed for pick random and random positions (default 1). The same seed always rolls the same numbers.

target.description: An amber target star on the stage at (x, y) — the "get the sprite to the star" goal. Mark it with run-program, observe ["position"], and a reference that lands on it.

oneOf.description: Read-only: pupils read, Run and Step but change nothing.
Values-in-slots: pupils retype numbers and text, pick from dropdowns and colours, but cannot add, move or delete blocks. The DEFAULT.
Adds a BUILD tab (and the full-screen builder): the palette (see toolbox), drag and drop across scripts, make a variable / list / block, add sprites, delete, Undo. The figure still opens on Run.

editable.description: The read / write / edit dial. Default "data". Use true only when building is the task.

toolbox.description: What the Build tab offers (editable: true). Default: "categories" on a MARKED figure — the whole categories its key uses — and "all" on an unmarked one. "blocks": only the block types the key uses. "pieces": a Parsons tray — the key's own blocks with their values filled in, each used once, slots fixed (the easiest rung). "all": every block. Or a list of category keys (motion, looks, sound, events, control, sensing, operators, variables, lists, myblocks, pen) and/or block op names and hat names.

distractors.description: Extra wrong blocks mixed into a "pieces" tray.

markFigure.description: Turns the figure into an AUTO-MARKED drawing task (responseMode run-figure; correctAnswer { derived: true }; editable must not be false). The pupil builds a program and presses Run; the drawing their pen makes is compared with this SHAPE — any program that draws it passes (a repeat or unrolled moves, any colour), by default at any position and orientation. The question text must say what to draw: the model never draws the target. The target's ink comes from running the block program the shape implies, so it is always drawable.

shape.description: regular-polygon (sides, length), rectangle (width, height), star (points, length, step), path (segments).

length.description: regular-polygon / star: side length in steps.

step.description: star: how many points each side skips (default 2; must share no factor with points).

segments.description: path: the lines the drawing must have, [x1, y1, x2, y2] in stage coordinates (y up). Use whole numbers pupils can reach with go to / glide.

anchored.description: true pins the drawing to the figure's start pose (a task that says where to draw). Default false: any position and orientation.

require.description: Method facts that must hold: uses-repeat, uses-forever, uses-if, uses-variable, uses-list, uses-procedure (a custom block defined AND called), uses-broadcast, uses-clone, uses-event (a hat other than the flag), max-blocks:n.

markProgram.description: Turns the figure into an AUTO-MARKED program task (responseMode run-program; correctAnswer { derived: true }). The pupil builds a program and presses Run; the model runs THEIR program and the REFERENCE over every test and compares what they DID — so any program that behaves the same passes, and one that hard-codes the shown case fails a hidden test. The reference is never shown (except as Parsons pieces when toolbox is "pieces"). Keep the visible program the TASK — empty, half-built or buggy — never the answer.

oneOf.description: A correct program as one green-flag script (the `script` shape).
A correct program in the project shape (several sprites or scripts).

reference.description: A correct answer — required unless every test carries `out`. A reference that fails to run leaves the tile unmarked with an authoring error, never a wrong pupil.

answers.description: Typed replies to the program's asks, in order.

hold.description: Hold the key this long (default 0.1 s) — for programs that poll "key pressed?".

events.description: A timeline of input for event-driven programs.

out.description: Optional authored expectation of what is SAID (say/think lines, in order); when absent it is derived by running the reference. Write a computed number as the bubble shows it: two decimal places when it is not whole (3.33, 0.50).

tests.description: The test battery (default one test with no input). The first is conventionally the case the question shows; later ones catch hard-coding.

observe.description: What must agree with the reference (default ["says"]): says (say/think lines in order), position (where each sprite ends), variables and lists (final values), drawing (the pen ink, exactly where the reference drew it).

seconds.description: Virtual seconds each run gets (default 10). A forever program is observed over this window.

require.description: Method facts that must hold: uses-repeat, uses-forever, uses-if, uses-variable, uses-list, uses-procedure (a custom block defined AND called), uses-broadcast, uses-clone, uses-event (a hat other than the flag), max-blocks:n.

text.description: Show the derived AQA pseudo-code under the scripts — shown only when the program has an AQA reading (one sprite, one green-flag script, custom blocks as SUBROUTINEs). Default false.

grid.description: Faint coordinate grid with edge numbers on the stage. Default false.

variables.description: Variable watchers on the stage (default true). Set false when they would give a predict question away.

lists.description: List watchers on the stage (default true).

controls.description: The Run / Step / Stop / Reset / Speed row and its full-screen button (default true). false (with editable: false) for a predict question that must not answer itself; ignored when editable is true.

stage.description: Only matters on a locked figure (editable false and controls false): default shows the stage only when there is something to read before running (motion, pen or pose blocks, several sprites, a backdrop, a target or grid). true / false overrides.

ran.description: Rest on the stage as the program leaves it, its drawing and the final pose, instead of the start: a solution figure that shows its answer without pressing Run. Run still replays it from the start. Default false.

header.description: Optional short title above the figure.

examples.label: Worked example — pen square: repeat 4 [move 100, turn 90]
Answer space (data dial) — edit the numbers so it draws a regular hexagon
Occluded question — predict what it says (count in threes); no controls
Hard case — a two-sprite catch game: arrow keys, clones, touching, a score and a timed broadcast
Build it, marked (run-figure) — an empty script and a derived palette: draw a regular pentagon with a loop
Parsons — the answer's own pieces, each used once, plus one distractor (run-program on what it says)
Events and costumes — a key walks the penguin with next costume; clicking it changes colour
